newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Generale Bank raises CFE to "buy".
newsitem.headline: Generale Bank raises CFE to "buy".

text.p: Belgian Generale Bank said in an investor note it rated shares in construction and dredging firm CFE a strong "buy" even after they posted a 9.27 percent gain on Thursday.
"For CFE we calculate a fair value of 14,250 francs, still 21 percent above (Thursday's) closing price," Generale Bank said.

Generale Bank said CFE's 39-percent owned dredging unit DEME was likely to record a 60 percent rise in sales in 1997 and record profit of some 1.3 billion Belgian francs and this was not fully discounted in the company's share price.
In addition, CFE should benefit from a speculative premium because of its status as a non-core business of the merged Suez-Lyonnaise group.
Belgian brokerage Corluy & Co said on Monday it rated CFE a "buy", estimating DEME's sales would rise 50 percent in 1997 to 23 billion francs with profit around 1.5 billion francs.
DEME's order book for 1998 also looked good, Corluy said.
Corluy noted that while Belgian holding company Ackermans & Van Haaren held 39 percent of DEME, DEME's weight in its portfolio was significantly less than in the case of CFE.
